diagnostic_conclusion: All30 candidate ID sets and22/24 evidence-complete case sets match Windows; exact contexts differ in all30. Changing only quantized engine to oneDNN did not restore parity in q001/q010/q024. Cause remains unisolated; no production code, engine setting, dependency version, model or reference result was changed to force a pass.

source_inputs.capture_scope: after build/probe and before result-document edits; installed Python hashes independently compared by probe

limitations: Windows prompt-context equivalence FAILED; this is not an all-checks-passed Docker result.
Linux retrieval evidence inclusion22/24 is not answer accuracy, grounded generation accuracy or refusal accuracy.
The published Windows API/Qwen generation scores must not be attributed to this Linux runtime; no Linux LLM generation was measured.
Search timings are small sequential HTTP samples on a shared workstation, with nearest-rank percentiles; no concurrency SLA or controlled cross-platform speed comparison.
Linux used quantized engine x86 and ONNX Runtime1.31.1; Windows reference used oneDNN and ONNX Runtime1.30.0. Matching the engine alone did not eliminate drift in the diagnostic sample.
Host Windows pytest252 passed; Linux performed actual HTTP/image/recreation checks, not full pytest.
Root base tag and some dependency ranges are mutable. Image ID, base digest and installed packages preserve this observation, not a future-build lock.
Only the isolated verification service was started/recreated/stopped; no pre-existing runtime was replaced.
